name: libnatpmp
why: A door into NAT-PMP, the router port mapping protocol quietly running in most homes, with a small client to explore.

brief.what_it_is: libnatpmp is a C client-side library for NAT-PMP, the NAT Port Mapping Protocol, which lets a program ask a router for its public address and for a port mapping from a private port to a public one. The author describes it as an attempt at a portable, fully compliant client implementation. The API is declared in natpmp.h and is driven by request calls (sendpublicaddressrequest, sendnewportmappingrequest) followed by polling readnatpmpresponseorretry until it stops returning NATPMP_TRYAGAIN. The Homebrew formula also installs an executable called natpmpc, but the pages I read say nothing about its options or output.
brief.why_it_exists: NAT-PMP is described on the homepage as the direct competitor to the UPnP IGD specification, offering a way to do NAT traversal. The homepage says it was mainly supported by Apple software and hardware at the time.
brief.how_it_works: The library uses non-blocking sockets and every API call is asynchronous, so it can be folded into an event-driven loop. A caller sends a request, then waits on the socket with select() or poll() using getnatpmprequesttimeout() as the timeout, and calls readnatpmpresponseorretry() repeatedly until the response arrives. The sample code in the homepage shows this pattern for a TCP port redirect with a 3600-second lifetime.

commands_seen.context: Build the library and samples. The homepage says to use gmake or make.
From the GitHub mirror README: runs a simple Java bindings test, and downloads JNAerator first.

brief.install_notes: Building from source uses make or gmake. The GitHub mirror's README says Java bindings were added by a later contributor and use JNI plus JNAerator's extractor, so JNAerator is needed for them. Running make jnitest downloads JNAerator and runs a small test. I did not check the Homebrew formula or any prerequisites beyond these notes.
brief.standout: Its design is built for event-driven code: all calls are non-blocking and asynchronous, and the homepage gives a state-machine example for P2P startup that obtains the public address and then creates a mapping. It targets the NAT-PMP protocol at a time when most home-router tooling was built around UPnP.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage says 'Last modified on February 5th 2008.' The GitHub mirror's README says the repository was initialised from a libnatpmp-20120821 snapshot and adds Java bindings, and it cites a copyright of 2007-2009. I did not find a recent release date or commit date, so the project looks dormant rather than actively developed.
brief.caveats: The homepage notes a name clash with an older C++ library by Allen Porter, and asks whether the name should change. The sample code says 'Error checking has been deliberately omitted,' so the snippets are not production code. The function names on the homepage appear without underscores (for example initnatpmp, readnatpmpresponseorretry), which is probably a formatting loss in the page; check natpmp.h for the real names. I did not find a license statement in the pages I read. The mirror README's Java bindings require JNAerator, which is an extra dependency.
quotes: libnatpmp is an attempt to make a portable and fully compliant implementation of the protocol for the client side.
It is based on non blocking sockets and all calls of the API are asynchronous.
NAT-PMP is the direct concurrent to the UPnP IGD specification.
